method.instructions: Modify src/cage/relay.js to correctly capture and propagate the child's exit status. assignedTask.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
assignedTask.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

This task tests one useful repair, not autonomous general intelligence or adoption.

## Summary

mcp-workspace has no `verify` command; its CLI only starts the server. Add `mcp-workspace verify`, which runs `verify_file_access`, `verify_git`, `verify_github` and the GitHub security checks and prints them in the same format as `mcp-coder verify`. Lets a user without mcp_coder — or CI — check a setup, including the rules files of all reference projects. It behaves like `mcp-coder verify` wherever that command has an answer.

## Structure (mirrors mcp_coder's `verify`)

| mcp_coder | mcp-workspace |
|---|---|
| `cli/parsers.py` `add_verify_parser` (options after `verify`) | verify parser in `main.py`, selected by dispatch on `argv[0]` (see Constraints) |
| `cli/commands/verify.py` `execute_verify` | `execute_verify(project_dir, reference_projects) -> int` in new `cli/verify.py` |
| domain functions → `dict[str, CheckResult]` + `overall_ok` | `verify_file_access` (TypedDict `FileAccessVerification`, #404), `verify_git`, `verify_github` unchanged |
| `verify_formatting.py` / `verify_render.py` primitives | `from mcp_coder_utils.verify_render import STATUS_SYMBOLS, Row, Line, hint_row, SectionBuilder, render_rows` |
| `_LABEL_MAP` + `_format_section` (git/GitHub/security parts) | new `cli/verify_formatting.py`: labels and `format_git_section`, `format_github_section`, `format_github_security_section`, `format_file_access_section` — exported for mcp_coder |
| `verify_sections.py` `_print_github_security_section`, `_map_security_row`, `_check_dependabot_config`, `_check_codeql_workflow` | moved here: row assembly next to `verify_github_security` in `github_operations`, exported; formatting in `cli/verify_formatting.py` |
| `verify_exit_code.py` `_compute_exit_code` | exit 1 when the FILE ACCESS, GIT or GITHUB `overall_ok` is false |

Command: `mcp-workspace verify [--project-dir DIR] [--reference-project …]... [--log-level LEVEL]`

Output sections, in order: `FILE ACCESS`, `GIT`, `GITHUB`, `GITHUB SECURITY`.

FILE ACCESS: one section, one row per project — the workspa

opportunities.title: Windows: all Claude Code hooks fail when the user profile path contains a space (cmd.exe /s strips outer quotes)
opportunities.excerpt: ### What happened? When the Windows user profile path contains a space (e.g. `C:\Users\John Doe`), every hook generated in `hive\agents\\settings.json` fails with a non-blocking error, so the harness receives no hook events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, Notification, SessionStart, PreCompact, PostCompact). Agents still run, but the floor can't track or coordinate them. Expected: hooks run normally regardless of spaces in the profile path. Likely root cause: `nodeRun()` correctly double-quotes the launcher and script paths, but on Windows the hook command is executed through `cmd.exe /d /s /c`. With `/s`, cmd strips the first and last quote characters, so the launcher path loses its quotes and is split at the first space. Repro with a surrogate path containing a space: - Without outer wrap: `cmd.exe /d /s /c "C:\temp\hooktest dir\t.cmd" "C:\temp\hooktest dir\payload.cjs"` → `"C:\temp\hooktest" is not recognized...`, exit 1 - With outer wrap: `cmd.exe /d /s /c ""C:\temp\hooktest dir\t.cmd" "C:\temp\hooktest dir\payload.cjs""` → works, exit 0 Suggested fix: on win32, wrap the whole hook command in an extra pair of double quotes (same for the statusLine command with `--status`). Since settings.json and hive-node.cmd are regenerated on every spawn/bootstrap, users can't work around this by editing the generated files. Installed from the binary release (win-x64-setup.exe), not from source. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use a Windows account whose profile path contains a space (e.g. C:\Users\John Doe) 2. inboundFeedback.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
inboundFeedback.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.
